title: Kinematics of motion in a straight line
overview: Use SUVAT equations, motion graphs and calculus to describe motion in a straight line, including under gravity. This guide turns the current syllabus outcomes into a connected revision sequence: learn the ideas, practise the method, then use the recall cards and checklist to diagnose what still needs work.
syllabusPoints: Use displacement, velocity and acceleration with consistent signs.
Use differentiation and integration between s, v and a.
Apply constant-acceleration formulae, including vertical motion under gravity.

definitions.definition: Signed change of position from a reference point.
Motion for which acceleration has a fixed value over the interval.

sections.title: Signs and variables
content: Choose one positive direction and keep it throughout. Displacement and velocity can be negative; speed and distance cannot. Turning points occur when v=0 and the sign of v changes.
bullets: State the positive direction in vertical-motion work.
A negative acceleration does not always mean slowing down.

sections.title: Motion graphs
content: Gradient of an s–t graph is velocity; gradient of a v–t graph is acceleration; signed area under v–t is displacement. Total distance requires adding the magnitudes of areas or splitting where v changes sign.
bullets: Horizontal v–t segments mean constant velocity.
An area below the time axis contributes negative displacement.

sections.title: Calculus links
content: Use v=ds/dt and a=dv/dt=v(dv/ds). Integrate acceleration to find velocity and integrate velocity to find displacement, applying initial conditions after each integration.
bullets: The v dv/ds form is useful when time is absent.

sections.title: SUVAT and gravity
content: Use v=u+at, s=ut+½at², v²=u²+2as, and s=(u+v)t/2 only on an interval of constant acceleration. For free vertical motion take acceleration as ±g according to the chosen positive direction.
bullets: At maximum height v=0, not a=0.
Use g=10 m s⁻² in this component unless told otherwise.

diagram.title: Kinematics of motion in a straight line: revision route

examTips: Write the selected SUVAT equation before substituting values.
Split multi-stage motion into intervals and carry final conditions forward.
Show the mathematical setup and exact working before the final rounded answer; unsupported calculator output may not earn method marks.
commonMistakes: Treating displacement and distance as identical.
Using a SUVAT formula when acceleration varies.
Changing the positive direction halfway through a solution.

quickRecall.question: What is the area under a velocity–time graph?
How is total distance found when velocity changes sign?
quickRecall.answer: Split at v=0 and add the magnitudes of the displacements.

quickRecall.question: What is acceleration at maximum height?
quickRecall.answer: It is still g downward; only velocity is zero.

quickRecall.question: When are SUVAT formulae valid?
quickRecall.answer: Only while acceleration is constant over the interval considered.
